EU-002.previous_note: The production picker now uses the Screenshot portal, then an owned frozen-image sampler. The sampler shows a 15x nearest-pixel neighbourhood, zero-based screenshot pixel coordinates, hex/RGB/HSV (HSB), pointer and one/ten-pixel keyboard sampling, a visible focus marker, explicit Use sampled colour and Escape/Cancel. The parent presents all eight catalogue formats (Hex, HexAlpha, Rgb, Rgba, Hsb, Hsl, Cmyk, Decimal) and coordinates; only explicit Copy controls write the clipboard. Cancel/Close preserves the previous colour and disposes screenshot pixels. Coordinates explicitly refer to screenshot pixels so no desktop/DPI transform is guessed. ColorPickerDialogTest names screenshotSamplingMagnifiesTracksCoordinatesAndCopiesOnlyExplicitly, screenshotEscapeAndParentCloseKeepPreviousColourAndDisposePixels, and screenshotPointerSamplingUsesSnapshotPixelsUnderScaledPreview pass alongside existing canonical-format/copy tests. PortalScreenshotTest adds screenshotColorPickerUsesPermissionPortalAndExplicitSampling and screenshotColorPickerCancelsPendingPermissionWithoutSampling against the existing fake Screenshot portal; those require the private D-Bus socket outside this sandbox. Keep partial until these portal integration cases pass and capture-permission review is recorded. Rationale: a frozen consented screenshot supplies actual sample pixels and coordinates that PickColor cannot return; no captured content is copied, saved or uploaded implicitly.

EU-003.note: QR generation rejects empty/oversized input and invalid output sizes, deterministically previews and explicitly copies/atomically saves/uploads through host controls with typed failures.

audit.coverage: QR generation rejects empty/oversized input and invalid output sizes, deterministically previews and explicitly copies/atomically saves/uploads through host controls with typed failures.

EU-003.previous_note: The encoder validates its input and produces typed failures: empty content and over-long content are refused, an invalid output size is refused, and the Reed-Solomon divisor, remainder, format information bits, version bits and capacity table are checked against hand-computed and published vectors. The render is deterministic, and the scannability oracle decodes the rendered PNG with zbarimg across every error-correction level and several versions, including UTF-8 content and capacity boundaries. The window supports explicit Copy to the clipboard, Save to a PNG written atomically through a temporary sibling, and Upload through a host-supplied port that receives an existing PNG path; the uploaded PNG lives in the dialog's own temporary directory and is removed with the dialog. A missing upload port leaves the action unavailable rather than failing.

EU-005.note: All six hash algorithms stream bounded chunks, expose progress/cancel, default SHA-256 and compare every digest digit without first-mismatch return.

audit.coverage: All six hash algorithms stream bounded chunks, expose progress/cancel, default SHA-256 and compare every digest digit without first-mismatch return.

EU-005.previous_note: The hash checker offers CRC32, MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, SHA-384 and SHA-512 and selects SHA-256 by default. Files are read in 1 MiB chunks, so a digest does not grow the reader's memory, and the known digests of an empty and a non-empty file are checked against published values and a large file matches a one-shot hash. Progress reports the bytes hashed and the file size, with an indeterminate bar when the size is unknown, and cancellation is polled at every chunk boundary so a cancelled read reports cancelled instead of a partial digest. digestMatches compares every digit and does not stop at the first difference, so the result does not depend on where two values parted; the length check is safe because the length follows from the algorithm.

EU-006.note: Native hash results identify file/algorithm and visibly label MD5/SHA-1 unsuitable for security verification.

audit.coverage: Native hash results identify file/algorithm and visibly label MD5/SHA-1 unsuitable for security verification.

EU-006.previous_note: A result names its algorithm and the file it came from, and the digest is presented as lowercase hexadecimal. hashAlgorithmIsWeak marks CRC32, MD5 and SHA-1 as unsuitable for security verification, and the hash checker labels a weak choice as unsuitable for security; nothing recommends MD5 or SHA-1 for an authenticity decision.

EU-007.note: Icon utility validates image/sizes, offers six sizes and palette8/truecolor32 modes, preserves applicable alpha and writes reader-accepted ICO only with selected entries.

audit.coverage: Icon utility validates image/sizes, offers six sizes and palette8/truecolor32 modes, preserves applicable alpha and writes reader-accepted ICO only with selected entries.

EU-007.previous_note: The converter validates the source image and refuses an invalid or oversized one with a visible error. It offers the six contract sizes 16, 32, 48, 64, 128 and 256 and both an 8-bit palette and a 32-bit true-color mode, and Save stays disabled until at least one size is checked. The container writer produces a structurally valid .ico: the header and every directory entry are well formed, a true-color entry keeps its alpha and a palette entry carries the expected header and mask, and the written file is read back and accepted by Qt's own 32-bit container reader. A cancelled save writes nothing, and a missing size list, an invalid size, an invalid image and a write failure each have their own stable code.

audit.coverage: Native converter exposes the exact fifteen contract codec IDs and applicable bitrate/output/folder/progress/cancel controls; requests reach every applicable codec.

EU-012.previous_note: The native converter exposes all 15 catalog codecs with compatible containers, input and output folder/name, applicable bitrate, progress, cancellation and explicit optional Show in folder. VideoConverterDialogTest iterates every codec and proves enabled bitrate values reach the conversion request, animated-image codecs disable and omit bitrate, and queued worker progress updates the visible control. VideoConversionTest checks catalog identity; existing dialog and integration tests cover success, cancellation and output. Without GStreamer the same registered command remains visible, disabled, and explains the required GStreamer core, base and pbutils components; ToolsFeatureUnavailableTest compiles and exercises that actual build branch independently of installed libraries. Rationale: retain the existing encoder-default bitrate and explicit Show in folder behavior, avoiding automatic folder opening.

EU-013.note: Structured GStreamer plans avoid shell interpolation and gate unavailable factories with hardware guidance; native atomic conversion covers installed codecs, not the complete hardware/driver failure matrix.

audit.coverage: Structured GStreamer plans avoid shell interpolation and gate unavailable factories with hardware guidance; native atomic conversion covers installed codecs, not the complete hardware/driver failure matrix.

EU-013.previous_note: codecAvailability never substitutes another codec: an unusable codec carries an actionable reason and the dialog lists it as disabled, so a hardware codec is shown only when it is usable. Command arguments are structured rather than built as a string: the pipeline description is path-free and names only src, dec, mux and sink, and the runner sets the filesrc and filesink location as a structured property, so a path cannot be injected into a command line. Output is written atomically to a hidden partial sibling next to the target and renamed only on success. The encoded argument is the structured properties of the plan, which is checked for the audio encoder and its dropped-audio diagnostic.

EU-014.note: Native plan validates input/container/codec/output conflicts and actual converter publishes atomically/removes cancelled partials; full codec/input/resource/output fault matrix remains incomplete.

audit.coverage: Native plan validates input/container/codec/output conflicts and actual converter publishes atomically/removes cancelled partials; full codec/input/resource/output fault matrix remains incomplete.

EU-014.previous_note: planConversion validates the container, codec and input combination and every invalid pair is rejected before a pipeline is built. The output rules never allow the input to be its own output and refuse an existing file unless overwrite is explicitly opted in, and suggestOutputPath reserves a non-conflicting name beside the input. The input file is preserved. A cancelled conversion removes the incomplete output, and the host result distinguishes Success, Cancelled and Failed through a dedicated outcome plus a stable error code. An existing output is refused rather than overwritten by default.

EU-015.note: Current utility operations keep input local and explicit output boundaries, but complete catalog retention/diagnostic/privacy contracts including blocked services remain unqualified.

audit.coverage: Current utility operations keep input local and explicit output boundaries, but complete catalog retention/diagnostic/privacy contracts including blocked services remain unqualified.

EU-015.previous_note: Utility inputs stay on the device. The hash checker reads the file and keeps only its digest; the colour picker keeps a recent-colour list inside the dialog; the image comparison owns a rendered snapshot and does not modify, save or upload either input. The one outward path is the QR Upload action, which is an explicit user action handing a PNG path to the host's own file-upload port, and the uploaded PNG lives in the dialog's temporary directory and is removed with the dialog. Diagnostics are stable codes without paths or content. QR scanning and OCR perform local decoding only, keep recognized data in an owned utility session and change the clipboard only through explicit Copy. They never enter capture save/upload/history workflows. Closing disposes the session; late workers and capture callbacks cannot republish values.
